t: A Polynesian society on remote Easter Island, settled around 1200 and organised in kin groups under a sacred paramount chief of the Miru clan.
Its people carved some 887 moai, mostly from Rano Raraku tuff, and devised rongorongo, the only possible script known from Polynesia.
Slave raids and epidemics in the 1860s reduced the islanders to 111 by 1877, and Chile annexed the island in 1888.
dyk: In the birdman rite, men swam to the islet of Motu Nui to await the first sooty tern egg of the season; the sponsor of the finder became tangata manu, the sacred birdman, for a year.
ev: Polynesian voyagers settle Rapa Nui; tradition names Hotu Matuʻa as the founder
Contact with Native Americans leaves lasting traces in the Rapanui genome
Jacob Roggeveen reaches the island on Easter Sunday, 5 April
James Cook finds that some moai have already been toppled
Peruvian slave raiders carry off or kill about 1,500 islanders
The missionary Eugène Eyraud arrives and later first reports the rongorongo tablets
Atamu Tekena and eleven chiefs sign an agreement with Chile’s Policarpo Toro

f.predecessor: Eastern Polynesian settlers from Mangareva or the Marquesas
